items.followUp: State two physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: Poor conductivity of heat or electricity is a physical property of non-metals.
rubric.description: Identifies poor conductivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-metals are poor conductors of heat or electricity.

rubric.why: These are other physical properties commonly associated with non-metals.
rubric.description: Gives another valid physical property.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one further correct property.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
Solid non-metals are brittle and are neither malleable nor ductile.
They are usually dull and non-sonorous.
(Any two properties.)

items.followUp: Describe one application each of Biochemistry and Industrial Chemistry.

rubric.why: Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and processes of living organisms.
rubric.description: Explains what Biochemistry studies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its study of chemistry in living organisms.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is used in medicine, including understanding disease and developing medicines.
rubric.description: Gives a medical application of Biochemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant medical application.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is also applied in fields such as agriculture and food science.
rubric.description: Gives another field in which Biochemistry is used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant application outside medicine.

rubric.why: Industrial Chemistry deals with manufacturing chemicals and products on a commercial or large scale.
rubric.description: Explains the scale and purpose of Industrial Chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing commercial- or large-scale manufacture.

rubric.why: These are examples of products or industries associated with Industrial Chemistry.
rubric.description: Gives examples of Industrial Chemistry applications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid industrial product or field.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and processes in living organisms.
It is used in medicine to understand diseases and develop medicines.
It is also used in agriculture and food science.
Industrial Chemistry deals with the manufacture of chemicals and useful products on a commercial scale.
It is used in industries that produce fertilizers, cement, glass, soaps, paper and textiles.

items.followUp: Compare Rutherford’s nuclear model with Bohr’s atomic model.

accept: most of the atom is empty space
rubric.why: Rutherford’s model has a small positive nucleus and proposes that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.description: States a central feature of Rutherford’s model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the positive nucleus or the mostly empty space in the atom.

rubric.why: Rutherford proposed that electrons move around the nucleus.
rubric.description: Describes electron motion in Rutherford’s model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons revolve or orbit around the nucleus.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability or line spectra.
rubric.description: Identifies a limitation of Rutherford’s model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant limitation, such as failure to explain stability or line spectra.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy specific orbits with definite energies.
rubric.description: States Bohr’s fixed-orbit concept.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fixed or stationary orbits or definite energy levels.

rubric.why: Bohr’s model accounts for stable stationary orbits and energy changes during transitions, explaining the hydrogen spectrum.
rubric.description: Explains Bohr’s account of energy and transitions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons do not radiate energy in stationary orbits, or that they absorb or emit energy when moving between orbits.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed that an atom has a small, positively charged nucleus and that most of the atom is empty space.
Electrons revolve around the nucleus.
Rutherford’s model could not explain why revolving electrons do not lose energy and fall into the nucleus, or explain line spectra.
Bohr proposed that electrons move in fixed orbits, each with a definite energy.
Electrons do not radiate energy in these stationary orbits; they absorb or emit energy when they move between orbits, explaining the hydrogen spectrum.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature, concentration and particle size affect the rate of diffusion in liquids.

rubric.why: Higher temperature increases particle motion and makes diffusion faster.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing temperature speeds up diffusion.

rubric.why: A greater concentration difference drives faster net diffusion.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of concentration difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a greater concentration difference increases the rate.

rubric.why: Smaller or lighter particles generally diffuse more rapidly through a liquid.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of particle size or mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that smaller or lighter particles diffuse faster.

rubric.why: Particles move more readily through a less viscous liquid, so diffusion is faster.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of liquid viscosity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that diffusion is faster in a less viscous liquid.

modelAnswer: Increasing the temperature increases the kinetic energy of liquid particles, so diffusion becomes faster.
A greater concentration difference between two regions increases the rate of diffusion.
Smaller or lighter particles diffuse faster than larger or heavier particles.
Diffusion is faster in a less viscous liquid because the particles can move through it more easily.

items.followUp: State four characteristics of a true solution.

rubric.why: A solution has uniform composition throughout.
rubric.description: Identifies the homogeneous nature of a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a solution is homogeneous or uniform throughout.

accept: cannot be seen with the naked eye
not be seen with the naked eye
rubric.why: Solution particles are extremely small and cannot be seen with the naked eye.
rubric.description: Describes the size or visibility of solution particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles are very small or not visible to the naked eye.

rubric.why: Solution particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.description: States that a solution is stable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles do not settle on standing.

accept: cannot be separated from the solution by ordinary filtration
rubric.why: Dissolved particles pass through ordinary filter paper and are not separated by filtration.
rubric.description: States the filtration property of a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a solution cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
Its solute particles are very small and cannot be seen with the naked eye.
The particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.
The solute cannot be separated from the solution by ordinary filtration.
